title: Jason Launches the Argo

scope.description: Jason gathers the Argonauts, the Argo is built, sacrifices are offered, and the expedition departs.

evidence.sourceText: Jason accordingly began to arrange his plans without delay, and invited the young heroes whose friendship he {216} had formed whilst under the care of Chiron, to join him in the perilous expedition.
When the vessel was completed, the Argonauts (so called after their ship) assembled, and their places were distributed by lot.

Jason now applied to Argos, one of the cleverest ship-builders of his time, who, under the guidance of Pallas-Athene, built for him a splendid fifty-oared galley, which was called the Argo, after the builder.

Jason now applied to Argos, one of the cleverest ship-builders of his time, who, under the guidance of Pallas-Athene, built for him a splendid fifty-oared galley, which was called the Argo, after the builder.
Jason was appointed commander-in-chief of the expedition, Tiphys acted as steersman, Lynceus as pilot.

Before their departure Jason offered a solemn sacrifice to Poseidon and all the other sea-deities; he also invoked the protection of Zeus and the Fates, and then, Mopsus having taken the auguries, and found them auspicious, the heroes stepped on board.

narrative.synopsis: Jason summons heroes for the Golden Fleece expedition, receives the newly built Argo, distributes the crew's places, offers sacrifice, and launches the voyage.
narrative.openingSituation: Jason begins plans to recover the Golden Fleece.
narrative.centralConflict: The expedition must be organized and launched before the heroes can seek the fleece.
narrative.resolution: The crew takes its assigned places in the Argo.
narrative.outcome: The Argo departs under Jason's command.
storyline: Jason arranged plans for the perilous expedition proposed by his uncle.
Argos built the Argo for Jason under Pallas-Athene's guidance.
The Argonauts took their places in the Argo and departed.
